scope: Controlled Day 12 pilot: Qwen3-0.6B-Base, one seed, two SFT mixtures, three supervised-token checkpoints, 28 dev cases per slice.

training_objective.objective: assistant-token cross-entropy on the scheduled SFT mixture
training_objective.schedule: linear warmup through 12,347 supervised tokens, then constant

training_loss.definition: sum(loss over supervised tokens) / supervised tokens

mixture_structure.format_observation: Finance targets repeatedly begin with 'Calculation:' and end with 'Final answer:'. Math targets use longer heterogeneous step-by-step prose. Equal token shares therefore do not imply equal behavioral or format influence.

paired_example.base: Long two-step reasoning: Amy has 70, then Lily plus Amy equals 120; parsed answer 120.
paired_example.all_sft_checkpoints: Emitted the finance-style 'Calculation:' template and stopped after computing only 50 + 20 = 70 (A-25 emitted a placeholder); all were wrong.

diagnosis.finding: Training-objective improvement and downstream-task improvement diverged.
diagnosis.basis: First-to-last-window SFT loss fell materially in both runs while every checkpoint lost 8-12 of Base's 12 math cases.

diagnosis.finding: The dominant failure mode is distribution/format overfitting plus capability interference, not an absence of learning.
diagnosis.basis: GSM8K outputs adopted the short FinQA program template and prematurely committed to one-step arithmetic; code improved early while math collapsed.

diagnosis.finding: Longer full-parameter training at a constant peak learning rate continued to move the small model away from its Base behavior.
diagnosis.basis: After 5% token warmup, 95% of tokens used a constant 2e-5 rate and every observed optimizer step was gradient-clipped; no decay or replay anchor protected Base capabilities.

diagnosis.finding: The exact checkpoint-to-checkpoint oscillations are not precisely estimable from this pilot.
diagnosis.basis: Each slice has only 28 cases and one seed, so movements of a few cases can be sampling noise even though the universal math regression is too large and consistent to dismiss.
